pr_title: Bluetooth: Keys: Fix BT_KEYS_OVERWRITE_OLDEST logic for BT_MAX_CONN > 1
pr_body:
When the Bluetooth stack is configured for CONFIG_BT_MAX_CONN > 1
the oldest key might currently be in use.  Fix the logic to ensure the
oldest key overwritten is from the set of keys currently not in use.

Fixes: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/35999

Signed-off-by: Faisal Saleem <faisal.saleem@setec.com.au>
Signed-off-by: Nick Ward <nick.ward@setec.com.au>
pr_comments: @jhedberg thanks for reviewing so quick.  I've added a commit on top of the previous commit (to remove ASAP) to show the changes when using the `bt_conn_foreach` but unfortunately it didn't get rid of the `#if ...` use as I had to re-introduce it when building with `CONFIG_BT_MAX_CONN==1`to fix the warning that the foreach callback wasn't used.  I also had to create a struct to pass in the key id and to get the 'in use' bool state out.  All up line count went up by 4.   See what you think, I'm happy to go either way.

I think the core of the problem is `bt_keys.aging_counter` which is build-time conditional. Otherwise we could remove most (possibly all) ifdefs by converting the code to use `if (IS_ENABLED(...)) {` kind of constructs.

Just a follow-up on IS_ENABLED() - when using that it's perfectly fine to have non-ifdefed static functions or variables which never get used in the end (because some Kconfig option is enabled or disabled). The compiler won't warn and they'll get stripped out of the binary. But as I said, we can't fully convert the code to follow this if there are dependencies to some build-time conditional struct members.
@jhedberg ok `#if ... ` use now removed and lines of code from beginning of pull request dropped by 3.  I'll repeat testing when I get a chance.
@jhedberg FYI I repeated my tests and the fix is still working.

issue_context.title: Unexpected Bluetooth disconnection and removal of bond
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
When using BT_KEYS_OVERWRITE_OLDEST=y and BT_MAX_CONN > 1 a connected device (if it is deemed the oldest bond) can be disconnected and bond removed.

**To Reproduce**
Use kconfig options with Bluetooth peripheral sample and protect the BAS characteristic with `BT_GATT_PERM_READ_AUTHEN`:
```
CONFIG_BT=y
CONFIG_BT_DEBUG_LOG=y
CONFIG_BT_SMP=y
CONFIG_BT_SIGNING=y
CONFIG_BT_PERIPHERAL=y
CONFIG_BT_DIS=y
CONFIG_BT_ATT_PREPARE_COUNT=5
CONFIG_BT_BAS=y
CONFIG_BT_HRS=y
CONFIG_BT_PRIVACY=y
CONFIG_BT_DEVICE_NAME="Zephyr Peripheral Sample Long Name"
CONFIG_BT_DEVICE_APPEARANCE=833
CONFIG_BT_DEVICE_NAME_DYNAMIC=y
CONFIG_BT_DEVICE_NAME_MAX=65

CONFIG_BT_KEYS_OVERWRITE_OLDEST=y
CONFIG_BT_SETTINGS=y
CONFIG_FLASH=y
CONFIG_FLASH_PAGE_LAYOUT=y
CONFIG_FLASH_MAP=y
CONFIG_NVS=y
CONFIG_SETTINGS=y

CONFIG_BT_MAX_CONN=2
CONFIG_BT_MAX_PAIRED=2
CONFIG_BT_KEYS_OVERWRITE_OLDEST=y
CONFIG_BT_KEYS_SAVE_AGING_COUNTER_ON_PAIRING=y
CONFIG_BT_FIXED_PASSKEY=y
```

Steps to reproduce:
1. Connect and bond device A
2. Connect and bond device B
3. (Note that device A will be oldest)
4. Disconnect device B
5. Connect and bond device C -> this will result in device A being disconnected and it's bond being overwritten
6. Try to reconnect device A and the bond will have to be made again to access protected characteristics

**Expected behavior**
At step 5 above although device A's bond is the oldest it is in use so should not be overwritten and instead device B's bond should be overwritten

**Impact**
Annoyance for end user

review_comments: really minor, but to keep consistent with other Bluetooth code: add an empty line after } unless the next line is also }

Hmm, if `CONFIG_BT_MAX_CONN == 1` then no keys can be in use. 

It's a bit difficult for me to fully understand if there are any side effect here, because I guess that if no keys are in use, then we possibly overwrite the key for the current connection. Is that safe to do?

The logic is if `CONFIG_BT_MAX_CONN == 1` then the bonding device is the only connected device which means all available key storage slots (1 or more) are considered not in use (by a connected device).  Note if there was a key slot previously used by the bonding device that would have been detected before the code above runs.  See:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/21ac7efc5c2629ca74d657bf52b0ed0a4ff62209/subsys/bluetooth/host/keys.c#L87-L89
Minor: The declaration of `struct bt_keys *key;` can be moved inside the first if statement to reduce the scope
Hmm, I left it as, although I can't find a reference to back it up, I thought the coding guidelines were to declare local variables at the top of function definitions.
You can leave as is; afaik we don't have any code guidelines for this, but some of the static code analysis tools we are looking into would probably require this at some point in the future
